# Native Manifold Marker Fitting and Independent Replay (Provisional)

## Model, Observations, and Clock

F03 reuses the F05c/F05d synthetic MuJoCo 3.8.0 floating-root plant and
bounded Crocoddyl BoxFDDP action. The compiled model has $n_q=9$, $n_v=8$,
$n_u=2$, two direct hinge torque motors, no root motor and a native Euler
step of $0.01\,\mathrm{s}$. It has no gravity, ground contact, grip, muscles
or human anatomy. Two named sites on the linked bodies serve as synthetic
world-frame markers. Their targets come from an independent native forward
run driven by a constant $(0.75,-0.5)\,\mathrm{N\,m}$ teacher. The optimizer
receives only site positions at native step boundaries, an explicit ordered
site list, metres, a world frame, per-site positive weights and a visibility
mask. It does not receive the teacher's state or input trajectory. One of
16 site-time observations is masked; an all-missing time row is rejected.

The marker clock is required to equal the native execution grid exactly
within $10^{-12}\,\mathrm{s}$. The observation hash binds that clock, ordered
sites, frame, visible positions, mask and weights. No interpolation of the
capture or commanded torque occurs in this fixture. A real capture clock
would need the separate F09 observation alignment, with its own exact
source-time and output-time identities. Its result is not supplied here.

## Tangent Observation Cost and Derivatives

Let $p_j(x_{k+1})$ be the native world position of site $j$ after one
MuJoCo Euler step, $y_{k+1,j}$ its target, $m_{k+1,j}\in\{0,1\}$ the
visibility mask and $w_j>0$ its weight. The running observation cost is

$$
\ell_{k+1}^{\mathrm{marker}}
=\sum_j m_{k+1,j}w_j\|p_j(x_{k+1})-y_{k+1,j}\|_2^2.
$$

The physical state is $x=[q_{9},v_{8}]\in\mathbb R^{17}$, but its local
tangent is $\delta x=[\delta q_{8},\delta v_{8}]\in\mathbb R^{16}$.
MuJoCo's `mj_jacSite` supplies $J_j=\partial p_j/\partial\delta q$;
the velocity columns of the immediate marker Jacobian are zero. For
$r_j=p_j-y_j$ and $\bar J_j=[J_j\;0]$, the local gradient and
Gauss–Newton curvature are

$$
g_p=2\sum_j m_j w_j\bar J_j^\mathsf T r_j,
\qquad
H_p=2\sum_j m_j w_j\bar J_j^\mathsf T\bar J_j.
$$

The F05c native discrete tangent derivative of the **same** Euler step
provides $(A_k,B_k)=\partial x_{k+1}/\partial(x_k,u_k)$ on that manifold.
The F05d action adds $A_k^\mathsf T g_p$ and $B_k^\mathsf T g_p$ to its
state and input gradients, and the corresponding $A_k,B_k$ sandwich of
$H_p$ to its Gauss–Newton Hessian blocks. It also adds the marker cost to
the independently evaluated nonlinear plan score, including the terminal
site observation. Finite differences of `mj_integratePos` perturbations
check both the site tangent gradient and the action's $x_{k+1}$ chain;
the source tests cover a masked site and input derivative separately.
The Gauss–Newton matrix omits second derivatives of site kinematics and
dynamics; line search and independent nonlinear scoring decide admission.

## Bounded Solve, Applied Input, and Evidence

The same exact initial native state and four-step control experiment are
used for the fitted controller and a zero-torque baseline. The optimizer
uses a three-step receding horizon, a 12-iteration cap, a cooperative
five-second **per-call** budget and small positive physical-state/effort
regularizers about the fixed initial state. This is a diagnostic solver
budget, not a real-time deadline. The F05d admission path checks motor
bounds, native nonlinear plan cost against the zero-torque fallback,
model identity, exact clock, hidden callbacks and contact-free policy.
Only an accepted first motor command reaches the plant. The F05d runner
exports the actual post-limit ZOH torques and complete initial
`mjSTATE_INTEGRATION` state through pinned Tools T01. A fresh native model
replays the saved history without the optimizer or observation feedback.

The supported-provider source-hashed receipt records four accepted commands
out of four in this particular synthetic run, and separately records that
the whole four-command trajectory was accepted. Across the visible site
coordinates the independently scored marker RMSE is
$1.71\times10^{-9}\,\mathrm m$ versus $8.88\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm m$
for zero torque. Complete-state replay differs by zero within a
$10^{-12}$ acceptance tolerance. The source-bound run measured
$0.78\,\mathrm s$ wall and $0.24\,\mathrm s$ process CPU for target
validation, controller
construction and derivative preflight, all native solves, execution,
baseline comparison, export, fresh replay and score validation in one local
run. They exclude the teacher generation, runtime startup and full
production data preparation. Warmup and machine load may change them.

These values establish only a reachable, contact-free, model-generated
marker fitting boundary. They do not demonstrate measured motion-capture
accuracy, marker attachment calibration, capture-clock alignment, contact
or grip feasibility, anatomical or muscle dynamics, robustness under
held-out perturbations, six-engine parity, or full-swing runtime. F03,
F05, F09 and the manual release remain open. The F03 turnover gives the
reproduction commands and exact source/input/observation identities.
